title: The CODI-CRAC 2021 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue
research_question: How can identity anaphora, bridging reference, and discourse deixis in conversational dialogue be benchmarked across multiple dialogue genres, and what performance do contemporary systems achieve under common evaluation conditions?
methodology: The organizers define three shared-task tracks covering identity anaphora, bridging anaphora, and discourse deixis, using ARRAU as training material and four newly annotated dialogue datasets for development and testing. The new datasets span AMI, LIGHT, PERSUASION, and SWITCHBOARD and are represented in the CONLL-UA format, with gold-mention and predicted-mention conditions provided for bridging and discourse deixis. Systems are submitted through CodaLab and evaluated with the Universal Anaphora scorer using task-specific metrics, while released baselines provide reference performance. The paper summarizes 115 runs from six teams and compares system performance across the four test genres.

key_findings.finding: The shared task establishes a multi-genre benchmark for three distinct kinds of dialogue anaphora: identity, bridging, and discourse deixis.
The newly annotated portion of the CODI-CRAC 2021 corpus contains 147,725 tokens, 41,807 markables, and 1,097 discourse-deixis instances across four dialogue datasets.
For predicted-mention discourse deixis, UTD_NLP obtains CoNLL average F1 scores between roughly 35 and 42 across the four sub-corpora, substantially ahead of the second submitted system.
In the discourse-deixis track, every submitted system reported in the evaluation outperforms the simple baseline on every sub-corpus.
Providing gold markables does not substantially improve the leading discourse-deixis system on LIGHT, AMI, or SWITCHBOARD, but raises its PERSUASION score by more than 12 CoNLL average F1 points.

Dialogue genre materially affects difficulty: the paper identifies AMI as especially challenging for identity anaphora because of annotation ambiguity and substantially longer conversations requiring longer-distance reference resolution.

The organizers caution that this first shared-task iteration is insufficient for broad conclusions about task or genre difficulty and identify annotation, scoring, and evaluation design as areas requiring refinement.

limitations: Because of time constraints, each newly annotated document was annotated by only one annotator, with spot checks by another annotator and an expert rather than full independent double annotation.
Participants lacked in-domain training data and primarily received out-of-domain training material plus in-domain development data, making the evaluation partly a domain-transfer problem.
Only two teams submitted discourse-deixis systems and three submitted bridging systems, limiting the breadth of comparisons for those tracks.
The organizers explicitly state that they had to address annotation, scorer development, and fair evaluation within a short period and could not resolve every issue completely satisfactorily.
The authors caution that it is premature to generalize strongly about task or genre properties from this first iteration.
Dataset accessibility is mixed: AMI, LIGHT, and PERSUASION shared-task data are freely available, whereas ARRAU and SWITCHBOARD are distributed through LDC under their respective access conditions.
raw_claims: CODI-CRAC 2021 evaluates identity anaphora, bridging reference, and discourse deixis in conversational data.
Four dialogue datasets were newly annotated for development and testing using an annotation scheme related to ARRAU.
The newly annotated corpus covers multiple dialogue genres rather than a single conversational domain.
Bridging and discourse-deixis evaluation include both predicted-markable and gold-markable settings.
The organizers released scoring and data-conversion scripts in addition to distributing the evaluation data.
A simple discourse-deixis baseline treats this and that as candidate anaphors and selects the immediately preceding clause or utterance as antecedent.
The leading submitted discourse-deixis system substantially exceeds the baseline on all four evaluated sub-corpora.
Gold markables do not yield uniform gains for discourse-deixis resolution across genres.
AMI contains longer conversations than the other newly annotated datasets and therefore creates more long-distance reference cases.
Each new document received only one primary annotation because of schedule constraints.
The organizers regard the first shared-task iteration as exploratory and call for improved annotation guidelines and further comparative analysis.
